raw_response:
I been planting cotton on this land for many many years. My man and me, we only got two hands each, but 20 mu is a lot. I do what my neighbors do, and what worked last year I keep doing.

For seed, I buy the Bt cotton seed — everyone buys it now from the shop in town. The old seed gets eaten by the bollworm too much, waste of work. Hybrid seed costs more but you don't lose the crop.

For fertilizer, before planting I put down compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, maybe 2 bags per mu, that's about 50 kg. Then I buy urea for topdressing when the cotton starts flowering, maybe one bag per mu, so around 40 kg urea. Last year I put a little less and the bolls were small, so this year I put a bit more. Better to waste some fertilizer than pick small cotton. I count it up: near 20 kg nitrogen for each mu, maybe 7-8 kg phosphorus, 7-8 kg potassium from the compound.

Water — I got the well, so I water before planting to wet the ground, then when flowering start, then when bolls fill. Three times, maybe four if the sky don't rain.

Spraying — cotton got many bugs. Aphid come first, then spider mite in hot time, then bollworm even with the Bt seed still need spray for the little worms that come late, and pink bollworm. I spray maybe 7-8 times the whole year, sometimes more if I see bugs. I go with my husband, we mix in the tank and walk the rows.

Before planting I plough the land deep with the tractor man from the village, pay him by the mu. Cotton need loose soil deep down.

Last year I picked about 270 kg per mu of seed cotton. This year I hope same or little more.
